findings.item: app.py role picker / _page_review / _approve; gate.py HttpGate shared credential
findings.problem: The role is a button click with no password and is never checked. Any role (pharmacist, ASHA) sees every patient's record and can approve/save. In live mode every browser user calls m5 as the single M6_API_USER, so m5 RLS, the physician-only save and the audit log see one identity.
findings.suggested_fix: Live mode: per-person m5 login, token kept in that session, role taken from the token; hide Approve unless the token role is physician; load the record list from m5 so RLS filters it; drop token and state on role change. Keep click-to-pick roles in MODE=mock only.
findings.evidence: RC-1: role=pharmacist approved rec-fx-asha-001 -> (True,'saved'). RC-2/2b: role=asha sees 8 records of 7 patient_refs and opened rec-fx-pharm-003-asr's transcript. RC-3: nurse -> asha with no password, Approve still enabled. Live part is code reading (UNVERIFIED).

findings.item: data.Catalogue in live mode + HttpGate M6_SERVER_IDS mapping
findings.problem: Live mode renders local fixture files but approves/saves the m5 row found through an id-mapping file. The human can approve a server record (possibly another patient's) that they never saw (CR-PATIENT class); reading also bypasses RLS.
findings.suggested_fix: Phase C: fetch the record via GET /records/{id} and the verdict via POST /records/{id}/verify, render exactly that JSON, send that verdict_id back; remove the mapping file.
findings.evidence: Code reading: data.py always reads fixtures/ and m6_ui/fixtures/; gate.py _post maps record_id -> UUID; m6 never calls GET /records or /verify. Not run live (UNVERIFIED).

findings.problem: m6 calls /approve before /save. m5's /approve sets status approved with approved_by and no flag check, so a refused save leaves the server record 'approved' while the UI says NOT saved.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Phase C adaptation call only /save (D-94: save = approve); m5 should remove or gate /approve.
findings.evidence: G-2b: after refused saves, mock gate status = 'approved'. m5 main.py lines 311-316 read; live behaviour UNVERIFIED.

findings.item: app.py result/edit state after a save
findings.problem: A second Approve on a saved record shows the red 'NOT saved' box although the record is saved; edit buttons stay active after save, so the screen can show a record different from the saved one.
findings.suggested_fix: When gate.status(rid)=='saved' hide Approve and edit buttons and show the saved banner; treat repeat approve as 'already saved' (green).
findings.evidence: G-4: first=(True,'saved'), second=(False,'error_other','already saved'), UI shows NOT saved, gate status saved. G-5: 2 edit buttons offered after save.

findings.item: app.py demo checkbox force_refuse vs env M6_MOCK_GATE_REFUSE (mock only)
findings.problem: The env setting documented as 'refuse every save' can be switched off by unticking a checkbox in the browser.
findings.suggested_fix: If the env variable is set, render the checkbox disabled (or not at all) and never lower force_refuse below the env value.
findings.evidence: G-3: env M6_MOCK_GATE_REFUSE=1, untick checkbox, approve rec-fx-asha-001 -> (True,'saved').

findings.problem: Unicode bidi override characters (U+202E etc.) pass schema validation and escaping, so a field such as a dose or patient_ref can be displayed reordered to the reviewer (display spoofing).
findings.suggested_fix: Reject U+202A-202E and U+2066-2069 in record/transcript strings (contract request) or replace them with a visible marker before rendering; keep ZWJ/ZWNJ.
findings.evidence: X-4: record.v1 with U+202E in patient_ref -> 0 schema errors; esc() keeps U+202E. Browser rendering UNVERIFIED.

findings.problem: An edited drug passes the mock re-check if it is any substring of the evidence span, so a one-letter drug is accepted and the mock gate saves it.
findings.suggested_fix: Whole-token match plus a minimum length or drug-lexicon hit; label mock saves 'saved (MOCK)'.
findings.evidence: G-6: rec-fx-asha-002 drug 'paracetamol' edited to 'ಪ' -> C2 pass.

findings.problem: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, so a page open in the same browser could frame the unauthenticated app and trick clicks (clickjacking). Cross-origin websocket is blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Put live mode behind a per-user login (F1); optionally serve through a local proxy adding frame-ancestors 'none'.
findings.evidence: H-6: GET / on 127.0.0.1:8501 had no anti-framing headers; WS-1: Origin evil.example -> 403. Iframe behaviour in a browser not tested (UNVERIFIED).

summary: Simulated AI security review of m6_ui (Streamlit 1.67.0) at commit 2f2fcfe. 31 concrete attempts: 17 AppTest attacks in mock mode, 10 HTTP/socket probes against two short local runs, 3 secret scans, pip-audit; m6 tests 105 passed. Held: XSS (all data escaped with html.escape before st.html, which also sanitises with DOMPurify; edit-form, server-message and card payloads stayed inert), forged click on a disabled Approve (server-side re-check), unknown/traversal record ids, static path traversal (400), query params ignored, cross-origin websocket (403), 127.0.0.1 binding in both launch paths, token kept server-side and only in the Authorization header, no secrets in tree or history (regex + exact .env match), pip-audit clean. Two major findings: the role is a click with no checks (a pharmacist saved a record; ASHA saw all patients), and live mode would approve a server record through an id map while showing a local file. Six minor: approve-before-save leaves 'approved' on the server, misleading state after save, env refuse flag overridable, bidi controls accepted, mock verifier substring pass, no anti-framing headers. Live mode, gitleaks and browser rendering NOT run (UNVERIFIED). No database started; both servers stopped.
